newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba economy will grow five pct in 1996 - minister.
newsitem.headline: Cuba economy will grow five pct in 1996 - minister.

text.p: Cuba's economy, recovering from a five-year crisis, will see Gross Domestic Product growth of more than 5 percent in 1996, despite the effects of Hurricane Lili, a Cuban government minister said.

Speaking at the annual Havana international trade fair, Trade Minister Ricardo Cabrisas said on Sunday that while the years since the collapse of the former Soviet Union had been difficult, the economy was recovering and "the target of 5 percent GDP growth this year will be surpassed."
GDP growth last year was 2.5 percent, according to authorities, following modest growth in 1994 and a contraction of more than 35 percent between 1990 and 1993.

Cabrisas pointed out that the fact the fair was larger than ever -- some 1,500 firms from 60 countries are taking part -- showed an eight-month old U.S. law reinforcing Washington's longstanding embargo on Cuba was not working.

The Helms-Burton law aimed, among other things, to discourage foreign investment on the communist-ruled island, by providing for sanctions and possible lawsuits against companies that do business in Cuban property formerly owned by U.S. citizens and nationalised after Castro's 1959 revolution.
The law has been widely condemned by Cuba's trade and investment partners such as Canada, the European Union and Mexico, which object to its extraterrorial aspects.

Vice-president Carlos Lage said last month the island should be able to achieve its 5 percent growth target for the year. Authorities appeared keen to show that despite the hurricane, prospects for recovery were not been crippled.
Hurricane Lili swept central and western areas of the country on October 17-18 and authorities said it destroyed 5,000 homes and damaged crops and power lines.
Cabrisas also said Cuba expected to be able to improve on the 1995-96 sugar harvest of 4.45 million tons (4.38 million tons) in the forthcoming sugar cane harvest. He did not give an official target.

The minister said that while the hurricane flooded cane fields and flattened some cane, almost all the flooded areas had now been drained. Sugar Ministry officials have said that despite the storm, most of the affected cane will be useable for the 1996-97 harvest.
President Fidel Castro formally opened the week-long fair on Sunday but did not make a speech.
